title: Pasta alla Norma
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Pasta alla Norma layers fried, silky eggplant into a bright tomato sauce, finished with salty ricotta salata and fresh basil — Sicily's tribute to Bellini's opera Norma.
longDesc: The eggplant is the star here, traditionally fried until deeply golden and creamy inside, then folded through a simple garlic-tomato sauce so its flavor permeates every bite, finished with a generous shower of shaved ricotta salata.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus more for frying the eggplant
Handful of fresh basil leaves, torn, plus more for garnish
100 g (3.5 oz) ricotta salata, shaved or grated
steps: Salt the eggplant cubes and let sit in a colander for 30 minutes to draw out excess moisture and bitterness. Pat dry thoroughly.
Heat a generous layer of vegetable oil in a skillet and fry the eggplant in batches until deeply golden and tender, about 5–6 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels.
In a separate pan, heat the olive oil and cook the garlic gently until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt, simmering for 15–20 minutes until thickened.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Fold the fried eggplant and torn basil into the tomato sauce.
Drain the pasta and toss with the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed.
Serve topped generously with shaved ricotta salata and extra basil.
chefTips: Salting the eggplant first is essential — it removes bitterness and excess water, so it fries to a creamy texture rather than turning soggy or greasy.
Fry the eggplant in small batches so it browns rather than steams.
Ricotta salata is distinct from fresh ricotta — it's pressed, salted, and aged, giving a firm, salty, shaveable texture.
commonMistakes: Skipping the salting step, leaving the eggplant bitter and prone to soaking up too much oil.
Overcrowding the pan while frying, which steams rather than browns the eggplant.
Substituting regular ricotta for ricotta salata — they have very different textures and roles in the dish.
storage: Refrigerate the sauce (without pasta) for up to 3 days.
reheating: Reheat the sauce gently in a pan, then toss with freshly cooked pasta.
healthBenefits: Eggplant is rich in fiber and antioxidants, particularly nasunin.
Tomatoes provide lycopene, linked to heart health.
culturalNote: The dish is named in honor of Vincenzo Bellini's opera Norma, reportedly after a writer exclaimed the dish was 'a Norma' — meaning it was a masterpiece worthy of the composer's finest work.
